chapter: Early recordings and arrival in New York
title: Coming to New York from Pittsburgh on a Sunday excursion
summary: She met Gladys Mosier in Pittsburgh and came to New York on a one-day excursion with little more than a cake of soap and a towel.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: It goes back farther than that. When I -- I met Gladys Mosier in Pittsburgh while I was working at the Benjamin Harris Literary Club.
And Gladys was the pianist of Ina Ray Hutton's band. So she had mentioned that --
Well, I mean all the musicians when they played Pittsburgh would wind up at the Benjamin Harris Literary Club because it was an after hours spot. And I got a lot of encouragement there.
But Gladys said, if you ever come to New York, look me up. So I had no address or anything like that. This was just a stroke of luck.
I came to New York -- I got off from work
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

like a Sunday Morning -- I came to New York on a Sunday excursion. And Jennie Dillard's brother -- he lived here in New York so he listened to the story, and he said he'd be looking for Gladys Mosier.
It was just by luck the band was playing at the Paramount Theater. I mean, this has got to be luck.
Did you buy a round-trip ticket?
Yes, I still have the other half. Oh yeah.

In fact, I didn't bring anything with me but a cake of soap and a towel. When I left, the only person that knew I was coming to New York was the waiter. His name was Obie, at the club. And he was a fan of mine. He was responsible for bringing a lot of musicians up there to hear me.
And I told him -- I said, "Look, I'm going to New York. And if I make it, I won't be back. But if I don't make it, I'll be back Monday night."
So, he was the only one that knew that I had gone. We finally found out that Gladys was at

the theater. We talked with her on the phone. I called her up and told her where I was, and she said, "Maxine who?" She didn't remember. It had been maybe six months, or more than that.
